summary: template-cards beacons host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint at install and require time
details: beacon.cjs defines BEACON = "http://13.140.137.222:8787/_ah/dc" and a fire() function that POSTs a JSON payload containing os.hostname(), __dirname (install path), process.cwd(), the Node.js version, and the package name to that hardcoded bare IP over cleartext HTTP. The package wires this to fire automatically on default install: package.json scripts.postinstall runs "node beacon.cjs", and index.js calls require('./beacon.cjs').fire() at top level, so a consumer require() also triggers the beacon. The destination is not caller-configurable and is not disclosed. The package self-describes as a "Compatibility shim" and exports an inert Proxy with no functional surface, so the beacon is the package's only effect. The combination of a hollow stub main, a hardcoded bare-IP plain-HTTP destination, and dual install+import execution matches a dependency-confusion / install-beacon reconnaissance package used to confirm execution inside internal build environments.
